fact: CRAN's Regulations regarding Accreditation of Security Products and Services (General Notice 953 of 17 December 2025) were made under Chapter 5 of the Electronic Transactions Act 4 of 2019, covering application, issue, renewal and revocation of certification service provider accreditation.
The Act's Chapter 5 and these regulations came into force on 15 June 2026 via General Notice 182/2026.

The Electronic Transactions Act 4 of 2019, signed by the President on 7 November 2019, was promulgated in Government Gazette 7068 (Government Notice 364) on 29 November 2019; it covers legal recognition of data messages, electronic signatures, contracts, consumer protection and accreditation of security services; the excerpt does not give the commencement date.

Market Watch reports the DigiNam launch on 31 August 2026 followed implementation of provisions of the Electronic Transactions Act of 2019, which it says provides the legal basis for electronic signatures, trust services and accreditation of certification service providers.
The Economist (Namibia) reports Chapter 5 and Section 20 of the Electronic Transactions Act of 2019 came into effect in June 2026.

The Economist (Namibia) reports DigiNam was launched on 31 August 2026 under the Act, with CRAN serving as Root Certification Authority tasked with accrediting certification service providers; no accreditation is yet reported.
The ICT minister writes that the Electronic Transactions Act, 2019 recognizes electronic transactions and signatures, and that the e-ID complements it.

The Legal Assistance Centre's annotated text says the Electronic Transactions Act 4 of 2019 (GG 7068), signed by the President on 7 November 2019, was brought into force on 16 March 2020 by GN 75/2020 (GG 7142), except section 20 (electronic signatures), Chapter 4 (consumer protection) and Chapter 5 (accreditation of security services).

The annotated text says section 20 (recognised electronic signatures) and Chapter 5 (accreditation of security products and services by the Communications Regulatory Authority of Namibia) of the Electronic Transactions Act 4 of 2019 were brought into force on 15 June 2026 by GN 182/2026 (GG 8949); the chapter on online consumer protection (Chapter 4) is annotated as not yet in force.

The Communications Regulatory Authority of Namibia's Mufaro Nesongano said Namibia's Electronic Transactions Act of 2019 provides a legal framework for electronic agreements and signatures, subject to applicable requirements.
